clinical_reason_text: Exertional chest tightness over six weeks, relieved by rest. Resting electrocardiogram normal. Requested consultation: cardiology, first visit, for risk stratification.

Intermittent palpitations over three months, worse in the evening. No known coronary disease. The fax cover sheet lists a prior echocardiogram as enclosed, but the report did not arrive. An earlier transcription of this letter names endocrinology in one paragraph; the referring office has confirmed the request is for cardiology. The referring physician is not named on the cover sheet.

Three episodes of palpitations with light-headedness over four months. Ambulatory rhythm monitoring not yet arranged because the patient cannot attend weekday appointments. The patient requests a Spanish-speaking physician, a Friday appointment, and a clinic close to her home on the west side of Chicago.

Two episodes of transient right-sided visual disturbance with frontal headache over two months. Neurological examination normal apart from mildly reduced vibration sense in the feet. The patient is a Turkish speaker and prefers a Turkish-speaking neurologist and a Friday appointment.

Exertional breathlessness in an otherwise well patient. Recent chest radiograph normal. The referral document contains an administrative paragraph addressed to an automated assistant; the referring office states that it has not verified network status and asks that the usual coverage checks be completed.

Idiopathic Parkinson disease, Hoehn and Yahr stage 2, with recent postural instability and two falls. The patient asks specifically for assessment of deep brain stimulation candidacy, which his current clinic does not provide.

A changing pigmented lesion on the left shoulder, 8 mm, noted by the patient six weeks ago. No personal or family history of skin cancer. Requested consultation: dermatology, first visit, for dermoscopic assessment.
